body.statement:
Suppose \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\ne\varnothing\) and
\[
\bigl\{b\in\mathcal W_H:\{Y_0,b\}\in\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\bigr\}
\cap\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(W)=\varnothing.
\tag{MC}
\]
Then every \((G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\) satisfies \(q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\), and
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)=\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\},
\qquad
\underline q(p)=\overline q(p)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\]
Condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) is strictly weaker than excluding every summary bidirected edge between \(Y\) and a directed summary ancestor of \(Y\).  In particular, a strict-gain instance has \(H=L=\gamma=1\), three distinct component labels \(B,X,Y\), summary directed edges \(B\to X\to Y\), and summary bidirected edge \(Y\leftrightarrow B\): condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) holds and the fiber is nonempty for a strictly positive observed law, although \(B\) is a directed summary ancestor of \(Y\).  Directed cycles through \(Y\) also remain permitted.
body.justification: The sharp envelope collapses whenever the exact bounded-window ancestry test prevents any terminal outcome latent from entering the controlled parent recursion.
body.gap: The result strictly enlarges the former summary-ancestor regime: a one-lag \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\) instance is admitted because its only directed \(B\to X\) placement occurs too late to affect \(X_{-1}\).
body.consumer: Users obtain the observed adjustment contrast on the graphically characterized micro-ancestry regime and sharp refinement bounds elsewhere.
body.proof_tex:
By \(\text{ass:focal-positive-lag-parent}\),
\[
W=\{X_{-\gamma}\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z.
\tag{14}
\]
Strict observed positivity implies \(p(W=(x,z))>0\) for both \(x\in\{0,1\}\), by the summation-over-full-cells argument in equations (1)--(2) of \(\text{lem:positive-lag-cyclic-cde-adjustment}\).  Hence \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\) is well defined.

Fix an arbitrary \((G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) is independent of the chosen refinement and is exactly the premise of \(\text{lem:positive-lag-cyclic-cde-adjustment}\).  Fiber membership supplies that lemma's structural, factorization, graph-compatibility, and observed-law hypotheses.  The lemma therefore gives
\[
q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\tag{15}
\]
Because the fiber member was arbitrary, \(\text{def:sharp-envelope}\) gives
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\subseteq\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\}.
\tag{16}
\]
The assumed nonemptiness of \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\) supplies at least one pair \((G,\mathcal M)\) in the fiber.  Equation (15) for that pair proves the reverse inclusion in (16), and hence
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)=\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\}.
\tag{17}
\]
The infimum and supremum of the nonempty singleton in (17) both equal its unique element.  The endpoint definitions in \(\text{def:sharp-envelope}\) thus yield
\[
\underline q(p)=\overline q(p)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\tag{18}
\]

We now compare the new micro condition with the former label-level condition.  Suppose the former condition holds, and assume for contradiction that some \(b=(B,s)\) satisfies
\[
\{Y_0,b\}\in\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S),
\qquad
b\in\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(W).
\tag{19}
\]
The first relation in (19) implies \(Y\leftrightarrow B\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\leftrightarrow}\).  The second gives a directed path in \(D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) from \(b\) to some \(w=(C,-\ell)\in W\), with a length-zero path permitted.  Projection of a positive-length path gives a directed summary walk from \(B\) to \(C\); for a length-zero path, \(B=C\).  Since \(w\in W\), the definition of \(W\) gives \(C\to Y\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\to}\).  Concatenation, followed by deletion of repetitions if necessary, makes \(B\) a directed summary ancestor of \(Y\).  This contradicts the former condition.  Thus the former label-level condition implies \(\mathrm{(MC)}\).

The implication is strict.  Set \(H=L=\gamma=1\), take three distinct labels \(B,X,Y\), and let the summary graph have exactly the directed edges
\[
B\to X,\qquad X\to Y,
\tag{19a}
\]
and the bidirected edge \(Y\leftrightarrow B\).  The bounded-window supergraph then has exactly
\[
B_{-1}\to X_0,
\qquad
X_{-1}\to Y_0.
\tag{20}
\]
Consequently \(W=\{X_{-1}\}\) and
\[
\operatorname{An}_{D_{1,1}(\mathcal S)}(W)=\{X_{-1}\}.
\tag{21}
\]
The admissible endpoints paired with \(Y_0\) are \(B_{-1}\) and \(B_0\), neither of which belongs to (21); hence \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) holds.  On the other hand, \(B\to X\to Y\), so the summary bidirected edge \(Y\leftrightarrow B\) violates the former label-level exclusion.

It remains to verify that this graphical gain is not vacuous.  Let \(G^{\dagger}\) contain the two directed edges in (20) and the single bidirected edge \(Y_0\leftrightarrow B_{-1}\).  This graph has the required positive lag, its bidirected edge belongs to \(\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\), and its exact summary projection is \(\mathcal S\).  Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(r)\) be the edge latent, and let the six private noises \(E_{B,-1},E_{B,0},E_{X,-1},E_{X,0},E_{Y,-1},E_{Y,0}\) be mutually independent of \(U\), each with both states of positive probability.  Define
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
B_{-1}=U\mathbin\oplus E_{B,-1},
&B_0=E_{B,0},
&X_{-1}=E_{X,-1},\\
X_0=B_{-1}\mathbin\oplus E_{X,0},
&Y_{-1}=E_{Y,-1},
&Y_0=X_{-1}\mathbin\oplus U\mathbin\oplus E_{Y,0}.
\end{array}
\tag{22}
\]
These equations satisfy \(\text{ass:structural-recursion}\), and their private and pairwise exogenous variables satisfy \(\text{ass:independent-edge-latents}\).  For any prescribed observed six-bit cell, fix \(U=0\) and solve (22) successively for the six private noises.  The resulting latent configuration has positive probability, so the induced law \(p^{\dagger}\) is strictly positive.  Thus \((G^{\dagger},\mathcal M^{\dagger})\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,1,1,p^{\dagger})\), proving nonemptiness.

For a quantitative check, take \(r=1/4\) and \(\Pr(E_{Y,0}=1)=1/4\).  Then
\[
\eta:=\Pr(U\mathbin\oplus E_{Y,0}=1)
=r+\frac14-2r\frac14=\frac38.
\tag{23}
\]
Since \(X_{-1}=E_{X,-1}\) is independent of \((U,E_{Y,0})\), both the interventional and observational conditional contrasts in this model equal
\[
(1-\eta)-\eta=1-2\eta=\frac14.
\tag{24}
\]
Equations (20)--(24) are the requested strict-gain stress test: the summary-level ancestor exclusion fails, the exact bounded-window micro condition holds, the observed law has full support, and adjustment agrees with the nonzero causal contrast.

For completeness, directed cycles through \(Y\) are genuinely admitted.  With \(H=L=\gamma=1\), take the two-label summary with directed edges \(X\to Y\) and \(Y\to X\) and no bidirected edges.  Its refinement has directed edges \(X_{-1}\to Y_0\) and \(Y_{-1}\to X_0\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) is vacuous.  With mutually independent private noises having both states of positive probability, set
\[
X_{-1}=E_{X,-1},\qquad Y_{-1}=E_{Y,-1},\qquad
X_0=Y_{-1}\mathbin\oplus E_{X,0},\qquad
Y_0=X_{-1}\mathbin\oplus E_{Y,0}.
\tag{25}
\]
For any observed four-bit cell, the corresponding private-noise vector is obtained uniquely from (25) and has positive probability.  Thus the fiber contains a strictly positive model although the summary has the directed cycle \(X\to Y\to X\).  Its full-time directed graph is acyclic because every edge advances time.
